title: One-arm Pull-ups - C
texts: One-arm pull-ups and weighted one-arm negative pull-ups

This workout is designed to help you work towards consolidating your one-arm pull-up strength. This workout is designed for climbers who can already perform one-arm pull-ups but would like to be able to complete more in one set. This training helps develop maximal pulling strength for climbing.

Part 1 of the workout contains one-arm pull-ups. Use body weight or, if possible, additional weight to complete the workout sets and reps in good form in full.  During the last reps of the workout, you should be close to failure due to the high intensity. This will mean you are developing maximal strength. If you cannot complete the listed volume, reduce the additional load or return to progression B of this workout in your next session.

You can start the pull-up with a slight bend in your elbow if this is more comfortable. Switch arms between sets to create a rest period of 3-4 minutes between the same arm being used.

Rest at least 5 minutes before part 2.

Part 2 of the workout involves one-arm negative pull-ups. Using an eccentric (lengthening) movement will help overload the muscles further and help develop more strength. 

You should aim to increase the additional load on the body via a weight belt or harness. Start with a small additional load and increase this by a kg or 2 each session if you can complete the workout volume in good form. 

Pull up using two arms or stand on a block to begin the movement at the highest part of a one-arm pull-up. From the highest point, slowly lower down using just one arm until you reach a fully straight position. Keep alternating arms within the set. This means you lower on one arm, then the other alternating for a total of 3 reps on each arm per set. There are 3 sets in total.

A timer will help you manage your lowering time. Each rep is 5 seconds allowing for 2 seconds to pull up on two arms and 3 seconds to lower on one arm. There are 6 reps of 5 seconds per set (3 on each arm).
